title: Welcome-screen sample take-home figure is hardcoded and doesn't match the app's own math for the identical schedule
where: index.html:5721-5722 (welcome screen literal) vs sampleNet() at index.html:3416-3423, DIFF_DEFAULTS at index.html:686-697, default baseRate at index.html:2204
detail:
The obStep===0 welcome screen shows a static, non-computed figure: `
Sample · 72 hrs this period
` followed by `
$3,951
` (line 5721-5722) — literal strings, not derived from any function. The same '72 hrs / 6 shifts' scenario is independently defined a few hundred lines later in `sampleNet()` (3 night + 2 weekend-day + 1 base, 12h each = 72 hrs), which the 'done' screen (obStep 4) actually renders via `fmt(sample.net)`. Computing sampleNet() by hand with the app's current defaults (baseRate=65.15 at line 2204, DIFF_DEFAULTS night=+$10/hr and weekend-day=+$11.5/hr at line 686, federal 12%, state 2.5%, FICA standard 7.65%, no pretax/posttax) gives gross = 3*(75.15*12) + 2*(76.65*12) + 1*(65.15*12) = 5326.80, and net = 5326.80 - (5326.80*0.0765 + 5326.80*0.12 + 5326.80*0.025) = 5326.80 - 1180.04 = 4146.76, i.e. fmt() would show $4,147 — not $3,951. The two numbers disagree by about $196 (≈5%) for what is presented as the exact same 72-hour, 6-shift schedule.
failure: A brand-new visitor sees '$3,951' on the very first screen (framed as 'we do the messy math so the number's never a surprise'). If she continues through the full setup path (steps 1-3) without touching any rate, the 'done' screen a few taps later — using the same default rate and the same 72-hour/6-shift assumption — shows $4,147 instead. The app contradicts its own headline number within a single onboarding session, which is precisely the kind of surprise the product claims to eliminate.
fix: Either compute the welcome-screen figure the same way sampleNet() does (call the existing sampleNet-equivalent logic against current default state, which is already in scope at obStep 0) so the two screens can never drift apart again, or replace the literal '$3,951' with a value that is verified to match sampleNet()'s output under the current defaults. Do not hand-tune the string again without re-deriving it — that is how it went stale.
